name: Symmetrical queenless middlegame

plans.label: Induce the first weakness
plans.description: Small-advantage technique: press with modest threats until a pawn must step forward or a structure concedes a permanent target, then switch the pressure to it.

success.note: An isolated or doubled Black pawn exists on some file; the vocabulary cannot say it was induced rather than inherited.

plans.label: King to the centre while the enemy king stays home
plans.description: The queens are off: centralize the king a phase early and use it as a fighting piece while the opponent's still hides on the back ranks.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'King into the game', whose success was placement quality. It is now the contrast the plan itself draws: White's king stands in the central four files between the second and fifth ranks and Black's does not. The region is an authored choice, not a derived one, and the census cannot say the king is safe there. Original success note: 'King activity is placement quality, not a fixed square this vocabulary can name.'

plans.label: Neutralize at par
plans.description: Meet each active try in kind without copying moves blindly, and pay unavoidable concessions in the least permanent currency available.

success.note: Neutralization is duration, not a property one position can certify.

plans.label: Time the first asymmetry
plans.description: Symmetry is a stance, not a plan: prepare the pawn break that unbalances the position on your terms before the first-mover pressure picks the moment for you.

success.note: Which break, on which file, cannot be fixed in advance for the whole family.

watch: Which side runs out of useful neutral moves first.
Every pawn move: with queens off, each one is close to permanent.
Whether the kings can centralize yet or must still respect mating nets.
typicalMistakes: Copying moves past the point where symmetry breaks tactically.
Treating a queenless middlegame as an agreed draw and drifting into a squeeze.
Simplifying while slightly worse and paying for it in the pawn ending.

sources: UNGROUNDED: agent-authored strategic claims with no citation, engine evaluation, corpus frequency, or owner review; queenless-technique doctrine rendered from model knowledge.

Trigger narrowing: the trigger proves queenless with both sides keeping a rook and a minor piece; it cannot prove symmetry - the vocabulary has no pawn-count, material-balance, or file-by-file equality predicate - and it cannot mark the middlegame-endgame boundary, so deep endgames with rooks and minors still on also fire. The entry names the family; the learner must confirm the symmetry the name promises.
